title: MEM-STRESS: Longitudinal Field Study of a Wearable-Informed AI Chatbot for Stress Management
abstract: arXiv:2611.23691v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Stress is an increasingly prevalent concern, creating a need for accessible and personalized support. Stress-management chatbots primarily rely on what users report, which may not capture their physiological changes. Wearables capture these changes, but chatbots rarely use them as memory across conversations. We therefore present MEM-STRESS, a stress-support chatbot that turns a wearable ring's physiological data into a layered memory of daily records, baseline deviations, LLM-generated summaries, and uses it to drive multi-session conversations grounded in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT). In a four-week, non-randomized study with 60 adults, we compared MEM-STRESS (Treatment) with a chatbot remembering only past conversations (Control).   Memory shaped the conversations: The Treatment chatbot referenced participants' physiological features (e.g., activity in 71.8% of sessions) and suggested more body-related DBT skills than Control

translated_title: MEM-STRESS：基于可穿戴设备信息的压力管理AI聊天机器人的纵向实地研究
translated_abstract: 压力正日益成为一个普遍关注的问题，人们因此需要易于获取且个性化的支持。现有的压力管理聊天机器人主要依赖用户的主观报告，这可能无法捕捉用户的生理变化。可穿戴设备能够捕捉这些生理变化，但聊天机器人很少将其作为跨对话的记忆加以利用。因此，我们提出了MEM-STRESS，这是一个压力支持聊天机器人，它将可穿戴戒指采集的生理数据转化为包含每日记录、基线偏差和LLM生成摘要的分层记忆，并利用这一记忆驱动基于辩证行为疗法（DBT）的多会话对话。在一项为期四周、共有60名成年人参与的非随机研究中，我们将MEM-STRESS（实验组）与仅记忆过去对话内容的聊天机器人（对照组）进行了比较。记忆塑造了对话：实验组聊天机器人在71.8%的对话会话中引用了参与者的生理特征（如活动情况），并且比对照组建议了更多与身体相关的DBT技能。
tldr: 该论文提出了MEM-STRESS，一个将可穿戴戒指生理数据转化为分层记忆（包括每日记录、基线偏差和LLM摘要）的压力支持聊天机器人，通过基于DBT的多会话对话实现个性化压力管理，研究表明这种生理数据驱动的记忆机制使聊天机器人能够在大多数对话中引用用户的生理特征并提供更多身体相关的压力管理技能。
en_tdlr: MEM-STRESS is a stress-support chatbot that transforms wearable ring physiological data into layered memory (daily records, baseline deviations, and LLM-generated summaries) to drive multi-session DBT-grounded conversations, demonstrating that memory-informed chatbots reference users' physiological features in most sessions and suggest more body-related stress-management skills than chatbots relying solely on conversation memory.
